section: Mir Jafar, Mir Qasim and the Battle of Buxar (1764); Treaty of Allahabad (1765) and Diwani
subsections: Treaty of Allahabad (1765) - separate terms; chronology
Mir Jafar - two tenures, Dutch intrigue, concessions

accepted.s: The Battle of Plassey was fought on which of the following dates and at which place?
o: 22 October 1757 at Fort William
22 October 1764 at Buxar
23 June 1757 at Palashi
23 June 1764 at Murshidabad
accepted.x: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 at Palashi, also known as Plassey, on the Bhagirathi River.
accepted.tq: Use the date-place combination to distinguish closely related battles.
accepted.sec: Buxar vs Plassey - "most decisive battle"  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best distinguishes the Battle of Buxar from the Battle of Plassey?
o: Buxar was an open military victory, whereas Plassey was substantially won through treachery and conspiracy.
Buxar was won through a conspiracy, whereas Plassey was an open military victory.
Both battles were fought against the Mughal Emperor alone.
Both battles resulted immediately in the grant of Diwani to the Company.
accepted.x: Plassey was won through the treachery of Mir Jafar and other conspirators, while Buxar was an open military victory.
accepted.tq: Test the contrast between the two columns rather than recalling an isolated fact.
accepted.sec: Buxar vs Plassey - "most decisive battle"  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Plassey:
1. Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah with approximately 3,000 men against a force of about 50,000.
2. Siraj-ud-Daulah was the last independent Nawab of Bengal.
3. Siraj-ud-Daulah received French support.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Clive's much smaller force defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey; Siraj was the last independent Nawab and had French support.
accepted.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the inclusive code.
accepted.sec: Buxar vs Plassey - "most decisive battle"  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Battle of Buxar was fought against which combination of powers?
o: The Mughal Emperor, the Nizam and the Dutch
Bengal, Awadh and the Mughal Emperor
Bengal, Hyderabad and the Marathas
Awadh, Mysore and the French
accepted.x: The Company fought the combined forces of Bengal, Awadh and the Mughal Emperor at Buxar.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct multi-party combination from the comparison.
accepted.sec: Buxar vs Plassey - "most decisive battle"  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a consequence specifically associated with the Battle of Buxar rather than the Battle of Plassey?
o: The Company restored the privileges of the 1717 farman.
The Company obtained the zamindari of the 24 Parganas.
Mir Jafar became Nawab of Bengal.
The Company secured the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and made Awadh dependent.
accepted.x: Buxar led to the grant of Diwani over Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and reduced Awadh to a dependent position. The other consequences relate to Plassey or the Treaty of Alinagar.
accepted.tq: Separate the consequences of two closely connected events.
accepted.sec: Buxar vs Plassey - "most decisive battle"  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of the conflict between the English East India Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah?
o: The French refusal to obey the Nawab's order to stop fortification
Fortification of Calcutta by the English without the Nawab's consent
Misuse of dastaks by Company servants
Sheltering of the Nawab's enemies by the Company
accepted.x: The French obeyed the Nawab's order to stop fortification; it was the English who continued fortifying Calcutta without his consent. Misuse of dastaks and sheltering enemies were causes of conflict.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed statement among otherwise relevant causes.
accepted.sec: Buxar vs Plassey - "most decisive battle"  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Black Hole episode of June 1756, consider the following statements:
1. Siraj-ud-Daulah first took Qasim Bazar and subsequently captured Calcutta.
2. Governor Drake fled to Fulta.
3. Holwell was among the European prisoners confined in a small cell.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Siraj captured Qasim Bazar and then Calcutta, Governor Drake fled to Fulta, and Holwell was among the prisoners confined in the small cell.
accepted.tq: Test a sequence of related details through a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: Buxar vs Plassey - "most decisive battle"  [other exams]

accepted.s: The British used the Black Hole episode primarily as
o: a reason for supporting Mir Madan
a pretext for war against Siraj-ud-Daulah
a justification for restoring the 1717 farman
a settlement mechanism with the French
accepted.x: The British used the deaths of prisoners in the Black Hole episode as a pretext for launching war against Siraj-ud-Daulah.
accepted.tq: Connect an event with the political use made of it.
accepted.sec: Buxar vs Plassey - "most decisive battle"  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following persons remained loyal to Siraj-ud-Daulah and fought for him at Plassey?
o: Mir Jafar
Mir Madan
Rai Durlabh
Jagat Seth
accepted.x: Mir Madan remained loyal to Siraj-ud-Daulah and fought on his side. Mir Jafar, Rai Durlabh and Jagat Seth were among the conspirators.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the loyal commander from the conspirators by matching person and role.
accepted.sec: Buxar vs Plassey - "most decisive battle"  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the conspiracy surrounding the Battle of Plassey?
o: Mir Jafar — Mir Bakshi
Mir Madan — principal conspirator against Siraj
Holwell — Nawab's commander
Governor Drake — leader of the anti-Company faction
accepted.x: Mir Jafar, who held the office of Mir Bakshi, was a principal conspirator against Siraj-ud-Daulah. Mir Madan was loyal to Siraj, while Holwell and Drake were associated with the British side.
accepted.tq: Use the person-office relationship to eliminate swapped roles.
accepted.sec: Buxar vs Plassey - "most decisive battle"  [other exams]

accepted.s: Following the Battle of Plassey, which one of the following combinations of concessions was obtained by the Company?
o: Kora and Allahabad, together with the Nizamat of Bengal
Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and control of Awadh
The whole of Bengal without the appointment of a Nawab
Zamindari of the 24 Parganas, duty-free trade and resources to fight the French
accepted.x: After Plassey, the Company obtained the zamindari of the 24 Parganas, duty-free trade in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, and resources to fight the French.
accepted.tq: Group the immediate commercial, territorial and strategic results of one event.
accepted.sec: Buxar vs Plassey - "most decisive battle"  [other exams]

accepted.s: Mir Jafar paid approximately what amount to the Company after becoming Nawab following the Battle of Plassey?
o: Rs 53 lakh
Rs 50 lakh
Rs 26 lakh
Rs 1.77 crore
accepted.x: Mir Jafar paid approximately Rs 1.77 crore to the Company after becoming Nawab of Bengal.
accepted.tq: Distinguish similar monetary figures by associating each amount with its transaction.
accepted.sec: Buxar vs Plassey - "most decisive battle"  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Treaty of Allahabad was concluded in 1765 by Robert Clive after he had returned as
o: Governor of Madras for the first time
Governor of Bengal for the second time
Resident at the court of Shah Alam II
Governor-General of India for the first time
accepted.x: Robert Clive returned as Governor of Bengal for the second time in May 1765 and concluded the Treaty of Allahabad later that year.
accepted.tq: Link the treaty to the office and tenure of the British negotiator.
accepted.sec: Treaty of Allahabad (1765) - separate terms; chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was a term imposed on Shuja-ud-Daula under the Treaty of Allahabad?
o: He received Kora and Allahabad from the Emperor.
He paid an indemnity of Rs 50 lakh and received the remainder of his dominions back.
He surrendered all his territories to the Company.
He obtained the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
accepted.x: Shuja-ud-Daula paid a war indemnity of Rs 50 lakh and recovered the rest of his dominions, while Kora and Allahabad were given to Shah Alam II.
accepted.tq: Separate the terms granted to Awadh from those granted to the Mughal Emperor.
accepted.sec: Treaty of Allahabad (1765) - separate terms; chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Treaty of Allahabad, Awadh was converted into
o: a buffer state under Company protection
a Mughal jagir under Shah Alam II
a directly administered Company province
an independent French protectorate
accepted.x: Awadh was restored to Shuja-ud-Daula, subject to its becoming a buffer state under the protection of the Company.
accepted.tq: Infer the political status from the treaty's territorial and protective arrangements.
accepted.sec: Treaty of Allahabad (1765) - separate terms; chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In return for the grant of Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, Shah Alam II was to receive annually from the Company
o: Rs 50 lakh
Rs 53 lakh
Rs 15 lakh
Rs 26 lakh
accepted.x: Shah Alam II granted the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in return for an annual payment of Rs 26 lakh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Emperor's annual payment from the indemnity and Nizamat figures.
accepted.sec: Treaty of Allahabad (1765) - separate terms; chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Shah Alam II — confirmed in possession of the entire estate of Banaras
Balwant Singh — Zamindar of Banaras, confirmed in full possession of his estate
Shuja-ud-Daula — granted the Diwani of Bengal
Nawab of Bengal — received Kora and Allahabad
accepted.x: Balwant Singh, the Zamindar of Banaras, was confirmed in full possession of his estate. Kora and Allahabad went to Shah Alam II, while the Diwani went to the Company.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure person-territory pair and reject swapped treaty terms.
accepted.sec: Treaty of Allahabad (1765) - separate terms; chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the arrangements made for Bengal after the Treaty of Allahabad:
1. The Nawab of Bengal retained the Nizamat in the fields of defence, police and justice.
2. The Company was to provide Rs 53 lakh annually for the Nizamat.
3. The Nawab retained unrestricted control over the Diwani.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Nawab retained the Nizamat nominally, while the Company obtained the Diwani; therefore statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the Diwani-Nizamat division.
accepted.sec: Treaty of Allahabad (1765) - separate terms; chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following treaties in chronological order:
A. Treaty of Mangalore
B. Treaty of Allahabad
C. Treaty of Salbai
D. Treaty of Madras associated with Haidar Ali
o: B, D, C, A
D, B, C, A
B, C, D, A
D, C, B, A
accepted.x: The treaties were concluded in the order Allahabad (1765), Madras (1769), Salbai (1782) and Mangalore (1784).
accepted.tq: Arrange the treaties by their years, using the earliest and latest as anchors.
accepted.sec: Treaty of Allahabad (1765) - separate terms; chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which treaty was concluded in 1782?
o: Treaty of Mangalore
Treaty of Madras
Treaty of Allahabad
Treaty of Salbai
accepted.x: The Treaty of Salbai was concluded in 1782; the treaties of Allahabad, Madras and Mangalore were concluded in 1765, 1769 and 1784 respectively.
accepted.tq: Use the year-to-treaty pairing to distinguish the four treaty dates.
accepted.sec: Treaty of Allahabad (1765) - separate terms; chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the two periods of Mir Jafar's tenure as Nawab of Bengal?
accepted.x: Mir Jafar served as Nawab from 1757 to 1760 and again from 1763 to 1765, after the fall of Mir Qasim.
accepted.tq: Test the two-tenure pattern instead of treating the office as a single continuous term.
accepted.sec: Mir Jafar - two tenures, Dutch intrigue, concessions

accepted.s: Mir Jafar's second tenure as Nawab began after
o: the death of Shah Alam II
the Treaty of Alinagar before the Battle of Plassey
the defeat and fall of Mir Qasim
the appointment of Warren Hastings as Governor
accepted.x: Mir Jafar was restored to the office in 1763 after Mir Qasim's fall and remained Nawab until 1765.
accepted.tq: Connect restoration to the immediately preceding political change.
accepted.sec: Mir Jafar - two tenures, Dutch intrigue, concessions

accepted.s: Mir Jafar's intrigue with which European power led to the Company's victory at Chinsura or Bidara in 1759?
o: The French
The Portuguese
The Danish
The Dutch
accepted.x: Mir Jafar plotted with the Dutch against the English, but Clive defeated the Dutch at Chinsura or Bidara in 1759, after which the Dutch left India.
accepted.tq: Match the Indian political actor with the European ally involved in the intrigue.
accepted.sec: Mir Jafar - two tenures, Dutch intrigue, concessions

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a reason for Mir Jafar's removal from office in 1760?
o: He surrendered Bengal to the Dutch.
He supported Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey.
He refused to accept the grant of Diwani to the Company.
He could not meet the Company's demands.
accepted.x: Mir Jafar was removed in 1760 because he could not meet the increasing demands of the Company.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated cause rather than a later consequence of his rule.
accepted.sec: Mir Jafar - two tenures, Dutch intrigue, concessions

accepted.s: During his second tenure, Mir Jafar accepted which limitation imposed by the Company?
o: The transfer of his capital to Calcutta
A ban on collecting land revenue
A limit on the size of his army
The abolition of the Nizamat
accepted.x: During his second tenure, Mir Jafar accepted restrictions on the size of his army, reflecting the Company's control over Bengal's political and military affairs.
accepted.tq: Identify the concession that directly reduced the Nawab's military autonomy.
accepted.sec: Mir Jafar - two tenures, Dutch intrigue, concessions

accepted.s: Who among the following was the son of Mir Jafar and became Nawab of Bengal from 1765?
o: Najm-ud-Daula
Muhammad Reza Khan
Balwant Singh
Mir Qasim
accepted.x: Najm-ud-Daula, the son of Mir Jafar, became Nawab of Bengal from 1765.
accepted.tq: Use the family relationship and accession year together to identify the ruler.
accepted.sec: Najm-ud-Daula - Company control

accepted.s: Under the arrangement made in 1765, the defence and administration of Bengal were handed over to
o: the Nawab of Awadh through the buffer-state system
a Company-nominated Naib Subahdar, Muhammad Reza Khan
Mir Jafar as hereditary military governor
the Mughal Emperor through the Diwan
accepted.x: Najm-ud-Daula handed defence and administration to the Company-nominated Naib Subahdar, Muhammad Reza Khan, while retaining the Nizamat only nominally.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority actually exercised power rather than which office remained nominally.
accepted.sec: Najm-ud-Daula - Company control

accepted.s: The political position of Najm-ud-Daula after the 1765 arrangement is best described as
o: an independent Nawab with control over defence and administration
a nominal holder of the Nizamat after the Company assumed effective control
a Company servant without any association with the Nizamat
a Mughal-appointed governor with independent revenue powers
accepted.x: Najm-ud-Daula was left with the Nizamat in name only, since defence and administration were placed under a Company-nominated official.
accepted.tq: Distinguish nominal authority from effective administrative power.
accepted.sec: Najm-ud-Daula - Company control

accepted.s: Which development in 1772 is associated with Warren Hastings?
o: Restoration of Mir Jafar for a second tenure
Formation of Awadh as a buffer state
End of Mughal pretence and rule by right of conquest
Grant of the Diwani to Shah Alam II
accepted.x: In 1772, Warren Hastings ended the Mughal pretence and ruled Bengal by right of conquest.
accepted.tq: Match the administrator with the institutional change associated with his tenure.
accepted.sec: Najm-ud-Daula - Company control
